title: Resource Governance & Memory Bounding in gVisor (512Mi)

protocol_checklist.intent: Prove strict resource clamping and safe termination under stress via cgroups v2 and gVisor.
protocol_checklist.configuration: Sandbox pod configured with resources.limits: {cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi} on gVisor runtime. Monitored via Prometheus / cAdvisor. Evaluated on standard test run vs. intentional memory-exhaustion tensor loop.
protocol_checklist.reality: Standard test peaked at 285 MiB RAM (55.6%) and 380m CPU (76%), finishing cleanly in 42s. Stress test terminated cleanly at 512 MiB by cgroups v2/gVisor (exit code 137, OOMKilled) in 2.8s without host node pressure or swap thrashing.
protocol_checklist.lessons: Workspace Rust compilation requires 1.5-2 GiB; claims of compiling under 30 MiB or 512 MiB are unrealistic and apply only to running pre-compiled release binaries or lightweight Python tests. Real engineering requires publishing truthful memory profiles.
protocol_checklist.industrial_transfer: On shopfloor edge controllers, background AI diagnostic microservices must live behind hard memory boundaries to guarantee they never starve real-time machine automation loops.
